commonProblems.h2: Iveco eDaily Engine Problems - What It Costs to Fix & When Replacement Makes Sense
commonProblems.h3: The Iveco eDaily is a relatively new entrant to the UK electric van market, having launched in 2022, and its electric powertrain - comprising a 140kW (190hp) GE Wolong synchronous motor and modular 37kWh battery packs - is generally robust. However, as with any commercial vehicle, issues do arise, and when they do, downtime is the biggest concern for fleet operators. The most common replacement-driving faults fall into three main areas: electric motor/inverter failure, battery management system (BMS) problems, and ePTO (electric power take-off) malfunctions. Every replacement motor supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded internal components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below, we break down the real costs of repair versus replacement for the most common Iveco eDaily faults.

problems.group: Iveco eDaily Electric Motor / Inverter Failure
problems.h4: Iveco eDaily Electric Motor / Inverter Failure - Why the 140kW Motor Sometimes Fails
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 80,000 - 150,000 miles (reports vary; EV motors are generally reliable but inverter components can fail earlier)
problems.rootCause: The eDaily’s 140kW permanent magnet synchronous motor (supplied by GE Wolong) is paired with a power inverter that converts DC battery power to AC for the motor. Inverter failure - often due to thermal stress, capacitor degradation, or power electronics faults - is the most common "motor" failure point in EVs. When the inverter fails, the motor loses power entirely or enters a reduced-performance limp mode. Less commonly, the motor itself can suffer from bearing wear or rotor magnet degradation, particularly in vehicles used for heavy towing or frequent rapid acceleration.
problems.recommendation: On an eDaily worth £25,000-£40,000 (depending on age, mileage and battery configuration), inverter replacement is often the better value if the motor itself is undamaged. However, if diagnostic testing reveals bearing wear, rotor magnet issues, or internal short circuits, a full motor replacement is the only sensible long-term solution. We recommend a full specialist diagnostic before committing to either route - inverter repairs are sometimes misdiagnosed as full motor failure.
problems.cta: Compare rebuilt Iveco eDaily 140kW motor prices for your variant now

problems.group: Iveco eDaily Battery Management System (BMS) Fault
problems.h4: Iveco eDaily Battery Management System (BMS) Fault - When Battery Replacement Becomes Inevitable
problems.affectedModels: Iveco eDaily all variants (35S, 42S, 50C, 72C) with one, two or three 37kWh eBS37 battery packs (2022-present)
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 50,000 - 100,000 miles (BMS issues can appear earlier; battery cell degradation is gradual)
problems.rootCause: The eDaily uses modular 37kWh NMC (Nickel Manganese Cobalt) lithium-ion battery packs supplied by Microvast, with a modular design that allows one, two or three packs to be fitted. The Battery Management System (BMS) monitors cell voltages, temperatures and state of charge across the pack. Common BMS faults include cell imbalance (where individual cells drift out of sync), communication errors between BMS and vehicle control units, and temperature sensor failures. A new battery pack costs around £15,000 plus labour, though Iveco offers a trade-in value for the old pack depending on age and condition. The battery carries a warranty of 155,000 miles and eight years (100,000 miles on single-battery vehicles) with an 80% performance guarantee.
problems.recommendation: Battery replacement on the eDaily is expensive - a full three-pack replacement can cost more than the vehicle is worth. However, the modular design means you can often replace just one faulty 37kWh pack rather than the entire bank. If your eDaily is still under the 8-year/155,000-mile warranty, claim through Iveco first. If not, a specialist replacement of the affected module is almost always better value than a full pack replacement.
problems.cta: Compare Iveco eDaily battery replacement prices from UK specialists

problems.group: Iveco eDaily ePTO (Electric Power Take-Off) Failure
problems.h4: Iveco eDaily ePTO (Electric Power Take-Off) Failure - A Specialist Problem for Commercial Operators
problems.affectedModels: Iveco eDaily chassis cab and dropside variants (42C14E, 50C14E, 72C14E) fitted with 15kW ePTO (2022-present)
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 60,000 - 120,000 miles (dependent on usage intensity; vehicles with frequent PTO operation fail earlier)
problems.rootCause: The eDaily features a class-leading 15kW electric power take-off (ePTO) that can operate even when the main motor is switched off. The ePTO uses an electric motor to drive a hydraulic pump, but the spline connection design has proven challenging for some aftermarket pump适配. Common failure points include the ePTO control module (communication errors with the vehicle ECU), mechanical wear on the spline connection, and wiring loom corrosion that falsely signals PTO engagement to the ECU. When the ePTO fails, it can prevent gear shifts or trigger limp mode.
problems.recommendation: ePTO failure is a specialist problem - most general garages lack the expertise to diagnose and repair these systems properly. If your eDaily is used for tipper, dropside or other PTO-dependent applications, we recommend using a specialist who understands the eDaily's unique 15kW ePTO system. In many cases, a wiring repair or sensor replacement resolves the issue without needing a full unit replacement.
problems.cta: Compare Iveco eDaily ePTO repair and replacement quotes

problems.group: Iveco eDaily Motor Controller / ECU Communication Fault
problems.h4: Iveco eDaily Motor Controller / ECU Communication Fault - The "Limp Mode" Nightmare
problems.affectedModels: Iveco eDaily all variants (2022-present) - particularly vehicles with frequent stop-start urban usage
problems.rootCause: The eDaily's motor control unit (ECU) manages communication between the motor, inverter, battery BMS, and vehicle systems. Complex electronic problems can develop, often manifesting as intermittent loss of power, limp mode activation, or failure to start. Common causes include CAN bus communication errors, corroded connectors, voltage irregularities, and software glitches. Unlike diesel Daily models with EGR and turbo issues, the eDaily's ECU problems are purely software and electrical in nature - but they can be just as debilitating for a commercial vehicle.
problems.recommendation: Intermittent faults are the most frustrating - and they're common on the eDaily's complex electronic architecture. Before replacing any hardware, insist on a full diagnostic scan from a specialist with EV-specific diagnostic equipment. Many "ECU failure" cases are actually wiring or connector issues that can be fixed for a fraction of the cost.
problems.cta: Get an Iveco eDaily motor control unit diagnostic quote

problems.group: Iveco eDaily Rapid Charging System Fault
problems.h4: Iveco eDaily Rapid Charging System Fault - When Your Van Won't Charge
problems.affectedModels: Iveco eDaily all variants with 80kW DC rapid charging capability (2022-present)
problems.rootCause: The eDaily supports up to 80kW DC rapid charging (with 115kW on four-battery configurations). Charging system faults typically stem from the onboard charger module, charging port corrosion, or communication errors between the vehicle and charging station. Unlike slower AC charging, rapid charging generates significant heat and places stress on the charging electronics - repeated rapid charging can accelerate component wear. Symptoms include the vehicle failing to initiate charging, charging stopping prematurely, or the dashboard displaying charging system warnings.
problems.recommendation: Before assuming the worst, try charging at a different location - many "charging faults" are actually station compatibility issues rather than vehicle problems. If the fault persists across multiple chargers, a specialist diagnostic is essential. The onboard charger is a high-value component, but repair is often possible rather than full replacement.

faq.h2: Iveco eDaily Engine Replacement - Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Can you replace an Iveco eDaily electric motor?
items.answer: Yes, the Iveco eDaily's 140kW electric motor can be replaced. Unlike diesel Daily engines, the eDaily uses a GE Wolong synchronous motor (code 550002E) which is typically replaced rather than rebuilt.
items.cta: Compare Iveco eDaily motor replacement quotes from UK EV specialists now

items.question: How much does an Iveco eDaily motor replacement cost in the UK?
items.answer: Iveco eDaily electric motor replacement typically costs £4,000-£7,000 for a reconditioned unit fitted, or £8,000-£12,000 for a brand new motor from Iveco.
items.cta: Get a fixed-price Iveco eDaily motor replacement quote online today

items.question: How much does an Iveco eDaily battery replacement cost?
items.answer: Iveco eDaily battery pack replacement costs £15,000-£30,000+ depending on configuration. A single 37kWh module costs around £15,000, while a full 111kWh (three-module) replacement can exceed £30,000.
items.cta: Request an Iveco eDaily battery replacement quote from UK specialists

items.question: Is the Iveco eDaily electric motor reliable?
items.answer: Yes, the eDaily's 140kW GE Wolong motor is considered highly reliable with an expected lifespan of 350,000 km. Electric motors have far fewer moving parts than diesel engines, making them inherently more durable.
items.cta: Compare Iveco eDaily motor replacement prices from trusted UK suppliers

items.question: How long does an Iveco eDaily motor last?
items.answer: The Iveco eDaily's 140kW electric motor is designed to last at least 350,000 km (approximately 217,000 miles) under normal operating conditions, according to Iveco's durability testing.
items.cta: Find a reconditioned Iveco eDaily motor with 12-month warranty

items.question: What is the difference between Iveco eDaily and diesel Daily engines?
items.answer: The Iveco eDaily uses a 140kW electric motor (190hp) with 400Nm torque, while diesel Daily models use F1A or F1C internal combustion engines. The eDaily has no gearbox, no exhaust system, and significantly fewer moving parts.
items.cta: Compare Iveco eDaily motor replacement vs diesel Daily engine costs

items.question: Where can I get an Iveco eDaily motor replaced in the UK?
items.answer: Iveco eDaily motor replacements are available through Iveco main dealers and a growing network of independent EV specialists across the UK. Specialist EV workshops are often faster and more cost-effective than main dealers.
items.cta: Get an Iveco eDaily motor replacement quote from UK EV specialists near you

items.question: Does the Iveco eDaily motor have a warranty?
items.answer: Yes, the eDaily's electric motor is covered by Iveco's manufacturer warranty - typically 3 years / 200,000 km for the vehicle, with the traction battery covered for 8 years / 250,000 km.
items.cta: Compare Iveco eDaily motor replacement prices with warranty included

items.question: Can I fit a used Iveco eDaily motor?
items.answer: Yes, used Iveco eDaily 140kW motors are available, but they are less common than reconditioned units. Used motors typically cost £2,500-£4,000, but condition and remaining lifespan are difficult to verify.
items.cta: Find a reconditioned Iveco eDaily motor with full warranty and traceable history

items.question: Is it worth replacing an Iveco eDaily motor, or should I buy a new van?
items.answer: For most commercial operators, replacing a failed eDaily motor (£5,000-£12,000) is significantly more cost-effective than buying a new eDaily (from £85,000 + VAT).
items.cta: Get a no-obligation Iveco eDaily motor replacement quote and compare your options
